items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Lines 1 to 9 are read as an over-the-top viral claim, excited and dramatic. From the twist on, calmer and amused; the last two story lines are warm and admiring. Chars voices a funny cartoon character, short and punchy.
lines: Narrator
Did you know this is the only city where only women live, and no man is welcome?
Narrator
Yes, you heard that right. And the craziest thing? Zero crime, for forty-eight years straight.
Narrator
This one-thousand-acre land is run by over forty women, and they live entirely off-grid:
Narrator
solar power, gravity-fed water, and over eighty percent of their food grown right here, from potatoes to herbs.
Narrator
All for less than five hundred dollars a month... living like queens.
Narrator
But the most mind-bending rule? No boys can be raised here. Have a son, and the mother moves out, until he's old enough to leave.
Narrator
Not even the president can visit... unless she's a woman. No police, no sheriff, not one nine-one-one call since the nineteen-seventies.
Narrator
So can you move in? Technically, no. Not even for one million dollars. It's not for sale, it's invitation only, and every single woman must vote yes.
Narrator
This is Woman's Land, in Oregon.
Chars
[wise old owl, dry, unimpressed, peering over glasses] Hoo-ld on. I checked.
Narrator
Here's the twist: almost none of that is true. It's not a city. It was eight small farms in southern Oregon... the biggest, about one hundred and fifty acres.
Narrator
About four to thirty women each. No vote: at one farm, any woman could move in, for twenty-two years. And the boy rule? Each farm set its own. One allowed boys under six.
Narrator
But here's what is true. In nineteen seventy-six, women with almost no money bought one hundred and forty-seven acres of hills... and made them a home for women.
Narrator
Fifty years later, it's still theirs. Honestly? That's more impressive than any viral myth.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
